purpose: Documentation and prior-art notes gathered during the dir-stats verification (2026-09-27). Read-only research; nothing here was tested against iCloud or FileProvider directories.

public_api.ATTR_CMNEXT_RECURSIVE_GENCOUNT: Documented in getattrlist(2) on this host: 'the recursive generation count of a directory that has been marked as maintain-dir-stats in an apfs file system ... updated any time any child is modified ... If the directory is not marked maintain-dir-stats, a zero is returned.' No deprecation note. Requires FSOPT_ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED (always set by getattrlistbulk).
public_api.setter: No public header declares the maintain-dir-stats setter. Libc's libdarwin/dirstat.c includes <apfs/apfs_fsctl.h>, which is not in the macOS SDK; the SDK has no usr/include/apfs directory and no dirstat.h. apfs.util -M issues fsctl 0xC1104A71 with a 272-byte struct whose u32 at +4 is 1.
public_api.dirstat_np: Exported by libsystem_darwin but forced to the fallback walk by rdar://32794924 in the open-source Libc; DIRSTAT_FAST_ONLY therefore always fails.

prior_art.notes: Quotes Jim Luther (Apple, retired) that fast directory sizing 'never really was hooked up or implemented right'; the Finder team requested it and declined to use it. Constraints cited: must be enabled on a new directory before content is added; counts data forks only (no xattrs/resource fork); synchronous API with no progress callbacks.
2017-2018 thread: no public API to enable it; ATTR_DIR_ALLOCSIZE/DATALENGTH do not return subtree sizes; nobody could find a directory where it was enabled by default.
APFS Guide: fast directory sizing can be enabled on empty directories only (contradicted by observation: apfs.util -M succeeds on populated directories and the totals are exact immediately).
Sonoma users report fsck_apfs / First Aid warnings such as 'missing dir-stats object (id N) referenced by 2 files / directories' on the Data volume; exit code 0; moderators say ignore.

First Aid on a Sonoma Data volume: 'descendants (2727) of dir-stats object (id 272950) is less than expected (2729)', 'physical_size (6608224256) of dir-stats object (id 272950) is greater than expected (6580809728)', several more; Disk Utility performed deferred repairs. Shows maintained totals can drift on real volumes and are corrected only by fsck.

who_uses_it: On this host nonzero gencounts were observed by the sibling reviewer only on iCloud sync roots (Desktop, Documents, Mobile Documents; EF_IS_SYNC_ROOT set). XNU's namespace-resolver completion path (vfs_syscalls.c, nspace_resolver_completion_data.orig_gencount) compares va_recursive_gencount before/after a dataless-file materialization and fails with EBUSY if it moved: FileProvider/iCloud is the in-tree consumer. Whether FileProvider re-marks or clears the flag on a sync root it does not own was not tested (touching iCloud directories was out of scope).
snapshots_and_time_machine: Not testable here without creating snapshots on the internal volume (tmutil localsnapshot acts on all volumes). The APFS reference lists INODE_MAINTAIN_DIR_STATS alongside INODE_SNAPSHOT_COW_EXEMPTION as the two inherited internal flags; ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE excludes bytes retained by snapshots while the dir-stats physical size does not know about snapshots (it counts allocated data-fork bytes of live files). fsck strings mention clone-group and purgeable dir-stats xfields.

non_apfs_behaviour_observed.devfs: fsctl GET -> ENOTSUP (45); getattrlist returns no CMNEXT attributes (ret_fork=0)
non_apfs_behaviour_observed.read_only_apfs: mark -> EROFS (30); GET and gencount read work
non_apfs_behaviour_observed.sealed_system_volume: gencount 0; GET performs a kernel walk (624 entries in 6.5 ms cold)
